inspiration.observed_pattern: A contact report uses REGEXP_LIKE in a CASE expression to classify phone strings by several regular-expression formats.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as an independently authored contact-channel audit. Because MariaDB 10.11.7 does not expose REGEXP_LIKE as a callable function, the equivalent REGEXP predicate with an inline case-insensitive flag classifies service handles, while a filtered report separates valid handles, missing values, and malformed labels. The schema, patterns, values, and reporting domain are new.

fixture_notes: Contacts 701 and 702 match the case-insensitive handle pattern, contact 703 is malformed, and contact 704 is NULL. The audit keeps all rows in the classification query and counts only valid handles in the filtered report.
determinism_notes: All contact IDs, labels, regular expressions, filters, and ordering are fixed. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE service_contacts (contact_id INT PRIMARY KEY, contact_label VARCHAR(96) NULL)
INSERT INTO service_contacts VALUES (701, 'Ops-East-17'), (702, 'billing-west-204'), (703, 'ops east 17'), (704, NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT contact_id, contact_label, CASE WHEN contact_label REGEXP '(?i)^[a-z]+-[a-z]+-[0-9]{2,3}$' THEN 'valid' WHEN contact_label IS NULL THEN 'missing' ELSE 'invalid' END AS label_status FROM service_contacts ORDER BY contact_id
SELECT COUNT(*) AS valid_count FROM service_contacts WHERE contact_label REGEXP '(?i)^[a-z]+-[a-z]+-[0-9]{2,3}$'

checks.sql: SELECT contact_id, contact_label FROM service_contacts ORDER BY contact_id
